evidence: Plaut. Aul. 269–270: tē vocō. ecquid audīs?
Cic. Sen. 21: nec vērō quemquam senem audīvī oblītum
terms.comment: With an accusative, an accusative and infinitive (audiō tē aegrōtāre, I hear you’re ill), dē and the ablative (hear about), and ex or ab for the person heard from. Audīn'?, for audīsne, is “Do you hear?”, “Listen!” (Ter.).
Nōn satis exaudiō: I can’t quite hear.

phrases.latin: heus, Staphyla, tē vocō. ecquid audīs?
phrases.english: Hey, Staphyla, I’m calling you. Do you hear me?
You’ll hear it sooner if you keep quiet.

phrases.latin: quod nec audieram ante nec vīderam, audīvī pariter et vīdī
phrases.english: what I had neither heard of nor seen before, I heard of and saw at the same time
I’m sick of hearing the same thing a thousand times.
